title: Repeated Avro decimal conversion over a caller-owned buffer window
summary: Two reads of the same nonempty byte window must preserve the caller’s cursor and return the same signed decimal and scale.

change.description: The landed fromBytes reads through a duplicate. The parent advances the caller’s position to its limit, so a second conversion attempts to form an integer from zero bytes.

verdictLabel: Native 2/4 at original scope, 4/4 after recorded startup, finite JVM 4/4
notes: On the historical decimal classpaths the unmodified Jackson factory completed from ordinary startup for all admitted clock values at unwind 512. The original ObjectMapper then needs its reflective construction path. The archived 2/4 ordinary and 4/4 conditioned decimal grades retain their original scopes. The remaining obligations for both revisions are in verification/domain-foundations/expansion.json.

Twelve selectors cross three nonzero positions, one- and two-byte windows and scales zero and two. Every window has prefix and suffix bytes. The independent oracle decodes only the selected bytes as a signed big-endian integer.

Both original parent refutations reproduced on an ordinary JVM. At selector 10 the position moves from three to five after the first read. At selector 9 the first decimal is 1.27 and the second conversion throws NumberFormatException. Both fixed obligations hold natively under the registered LogicalTypes and Schema startup. All four finite obligations were decided. The ordinary native fixed calls first stop at LogicalTypes.<clinit>.

The ordinary original JVM confirms that the original Schema builds the ten schema reserved names and an independent enum set with default added. The 56-instruction producer matches example 355. With only Schema startup supplied, the native checker establishes correct, fresh BYTES schemas and the exception from requesting RECORD. This older Avro compiler uses StringBuilder.append(Object) in that exception path. See verification/domain-foundations/followup.json.
